TypedPayloadDescriptor.description: Current 24-byte profile and schema binding for one typed payload frame. It contains only fields present on the wire.

TypedPayloadFrame.description: Owned descriptor and payload bytes. Each descriptor carries one payload kind and the enclosing bitmap equals the union of descriptor kinds plus tensor when tensor regions are present.
TypedPayloadFrame.resolutionRule: Consumers validate payload_kind together with profile_id, schema_id, and schema_version. The payload kind is read from the descriptor and is never inferred from descriptor order or a multi-bit bitmap.

SchemaDescriptorHeader.description: Public 32-byte schema identity and compatibility descriptor. Profile-private schema bodies remain outside the public header.

SchemaRegistry.description: Host registry shared by all SDKs. Handles and FFI entrypoints remain internal.

RuntimeFrameHeader.description: Lossless projection of every non-derived NNRP common-header field.

SubmitHeaderContext.description: Caller-controlled common-header fields for FRAME_SUBMIT. The active session owns session_id and the request owns frame_id.

SubmitIdentity.description: Caller-owned identities and common-header context shared by every submit builder.

SubmitPolicy.description: Caller-controlled scheduling and recovery semantics shared by every submit builder.

TensorSection.description: Owned semantic tensor section. Builders derive descriptor flags, table lengths, payload lengths, and fixed- or variable-stride wire representation.

SubmitObjectReferences.description: Optional standard object-reference slots for tensor submits. Builders reject duplicates and derive submit_mode and object_ref_mask from inline values and references.

TensorSubmitInput.description: High-level tensor builder input. Tile, section, body-region, reference-mask, count, and length fields are SDK-derived.

TokenChunk.description: Owned token delta with frozen token profile, schema, and append-stream defaults.

TokenSubmitInput.description: High-level token builder input. The builder emits token typed-payload descriptors and derives the bitmap and frame count.

TypedPayloadInputFrame.description: Owned semantic typed-payload input. The submit builder derives descriptor offset and length from payload order and size.

TypedPayloadSubmitInput.description: High-level generic typed-payload builder input for token-independent typed profiles.

SubmitMetadata.description: Typed semantic projection of FRAME_SUBMIT metadata excluding operation_id, which is owned by SubmitRequest.
SubmitMetadata.builderRequirement: Every SDK provides tensor, token, and generic typed-payload builders. Ordinary callers do not populate wire-shape counters, byte lengths, or payload bitmaps manually. Direct SubmitMetadata construction is a protocol-expert surface.

SubmitRequest.description: Profile-neutral, owned, high-level role request. It never accepts an encoded FFI buffer.
SubmitRequest.ffiRule: Bindings encode metadata and body once and perform one coarse native submit call. The FFI carrier transports operation_id, frame_id, and SubmitHeaderContext together with the encoded metadata/body payload; Rust owns session_id and the derived header lengths. The carrier rejects operation_id disagreement with encoded metadata.

FrameSubmitMetadata.description: Complete FRAME_SUBMIT wire metadata, including the operation identity carried on the wire.

ResultPushMetadata.description: Complete RESULT_PUSH metadata. status_code is an application-defined u16 detail code and does not determine protocol terminal state.
ResultPushMetadata.terminalStateRule: RESULT_PUSH is a successful terminal result. Cancellation, drop, and error terminal states are determined by their protocol messages and operation lifecycle, never by status_code.

CacheObjectId.description: Cross-SDK cache identity. Language projections may spell the high and low key halves idiomatically but preserve their widths and order.

CacheLease.description: Validated local cache lease value. It is not a wire payload or native handle.

CachePolicyOptions.description: Explicit local cache policy. Disabled policy carries no reuse scope or expiration hint and never emits an implicit cache request.

NnrpEndpoint.description: Validated transport-neutral application endpoint. Only nnrp and nnrps schemes are accepted.

ProviderEndpoint.description: Validated provider-local locator. Its scheme must match the provider transport.

ClientSessionOptions.description: Transport-neutral application options. Session fields are normalized into SESSION_OPEN metadata, cache_hints contributes to the automatic CLIENT_HELLO cache bitmap, and resume_token_bytes is a local receive-capacity request. SDK-local handles and generations are forbidden here.

fields.name: resume_token_bytes
fields.description: Maximum opaque recovery-token bytes the client accepts; zero selects the runtime default. This is not the SESSION_OPEN resume_token_bytes field.

fields.name: cache_hints
fields.description: Connection capability hints folded into CLIENT_HELLO.cache_object_bitmap before the first session opens.

SessionRecoveryTicket.description: Runtime-issued opaque proof used to resume one session. Applications may persist and return the value but may not construct, truncate, inspect, or replace resume_token.
invariants: resume_token is compared as an opaque byte sequence
resume_window_ms records the negotiated validity window
the persisted encoding is canonical and contains exactly fixed_prefix_bytes plus resume_token_bytes

opaqueEncoding.name: NRTK
validation: the input ends exactly after resume_token

ServerSessionPolicy.description: Application admission policy evaluated once per SESSION_OPEN. The default policy accepts valid sessions.

ServerSessionOptions.description: Transport-neutral server negotiation, cache, credit, schema, and admission policy.

ServerAcceptOptions.description: Local accept wait policy. Native session handles and generations are internal.

RuntimeEventMetadata.description: Closed metadata union used by public role event pumps. The common header message_type selects exactly one variant.

RuntimeEventTail.description: Closed owned tail union. A tail never aliases a receive buffer or an FFI event handle.

RuntimeEvent.description: Owned event envelope shared by client and server role APIs.
RuntimeEvent.ownership: metadata and tail storage remain valid independently of the receive buffer and native event handle
RuntimeEvent.ffiLifecycleRule: A native event with header.present == 1 is a wire RuntimeEvent. A native event with header.present == 0 is a local lifecycle event and must remain in a separate SDK lifecycle-event type; bindings must not fabricate a RuntimeFrameHeader for it.

OperationLifecycleEvent.description: Local role lifecycle notification. It is never represented as a fabricated wire frame.

TerminalEvent.description: Closed terminal-evidence union. It preserves either a complete wire RuntimeEvent or a headerless local OperationLifecycleEvent without flattening or fabrication.
TerminalEvent.invariant: Exactly one variant is present. SDKs must not expose nullable parallel runtime-event and lifecycle-event fields.

NnrpResult.description: Application-facing terminal result correlated with one submitted operation. Its terminal evidence preserves either the complete wire event or the exact headerless local lifecycle event.
NnrpResult.successRule: A successful result has terminal_state success and an event whose message type is result_push and whose metadata variant is result_push.
NnrpResult.nonSuccessRule: Cancelled, dropped, and error results preserve the terminal protocol or lifecycle event that established the state; SDKs do not synthesize RESULT_PUSH metadata for them.

roleSurfaces.runtimeEventRoleBooleans: The client and server booleans on runtimeEventMessages identify receiving roles. The opposite role is an allowed sender.

client.connectionHandshake: automatic CLIENT_HELLO followed by SERVER_HELLO_ACK before the first SESSION_OPEN
client.sendMessages: all runtimeEventMessages where server is true
client.receiveMessages: all runtimeEventMessages where client is true
client.sendRequirement: Every allowed message is available through an ergonomic named method or a typed generic runtime-frame method. Raw message codes without metadata validation are not an application API.

server.connectionHandshake: accept and validate one CLIENT_HELLO, then emit SERVER_HELLO_ACK before accepting SESSION_OPEN messages
server.sendMessages: all runtimeEventMessages where client is true
server.receiveMessages: all runtimeEventMessages where server is true
server.sendRequirement: Every allowed message is available through an ergonomic named method or a typed generic runtime-frame method. Raw message codes without metadata validation are not an application API.

transportBoundary.rule: Application endpoints are transport-neutral. Provider locators remain provider-local and never replace the application endpoint.

providerBoundary.rule: A provider package owns real carrier behavior and its scoped artifact. Installing a provider is not a configuration flag over transport logic hidden in a client or server package.

publicOptionBoundary.rule: Public bootstrap and session options expose protocol intent. FFI handles stay internal, while application profile and patch values remain outside SESSION_OPEN options.
